enemy.definition: The feeling that there is no hope of things getting better.

goal.description: Later lexical blocks supply familiar rescue vocabulary.

notes: Every bundled dictionary spelling that fits the opening letter multiset is classified before solver search; no move, selection, vocabulary or state budget limits this audit.

The full opening-plus-refill multiset is an optimistic future spelling superset, not an enumeration of reachable boards. Refill order, consumed letters and remaining turns can make included words unreachable.
Unknown POS remains unknown and receives no inferred category. Unlisted semantics use the neutral gameplay fallback; absence from semantic lists does not establish unrelated meaning.
Counts describe distinct spellings, not physical tile selections. Single and multiple POS counts partition known spellings; POS membership counts can overlap.
FNV-1a fingerprints detect ordinary stale reports and are not cryptographic authenticity checks. Versioned lexical metadata records the source archive SHA-256.
Winning-line counts and viable openings are lower bounds from retained witnesses; they are not exhaustive path counts.
Reasonable play samples useful moves within an immediate-score margin, taking a fixed number per state; fairness is conditional on this sample.
The fixed fairness state budget alternates breadth and deepest pending positions, preserving early opening diversity while sampling late Resolve; this is not an unbiased random-player distribution.
Unknown bounded-search states are not counted as dead or safe. Fairness rates exclude unknown states and report an uncertainty interval.
Letter supply is an optimistic physical upper bound. Observed word opportunities are lower bounds and do not guarantee future accessibility.
Commonness is a local curated familiarity estimate; missing annotations remain unknown. Required vocabulary describes the best observed winning line.
Counterfactual replays are exact for the same tile-ID sequence; separate bounded searches compare witnessed solutions and cannot prove decorative mechanics unless exhaustive.
The strategic opening is from the best observed line. Immediate-move optimality is reported only when proved, using physical tile identities and minimum-turn wins.

Special preservation means retaining its physical tile, including an untriggered Strike tile. Automatic-opening claims require complete dictionary and tile-ID discovery within the reasonable-play definition.
Clutch lines may include additional exact winning witnesses outside the reasonable-state sample; those witnesses do not inflate the sampled final-turn rescue rate.
REGEN recovery is resolved after damage in every searched state. Its importance measures observed route changes; avoiding the harmful tile can itself be a valid strategy.

Winning witnesses retain distinct opening, semantic-pattern and special-timing strategies. Counterfactuals replay the same diverse sample of at most six prefixes and finishes for every mechanic; final-word variants do not crowd out distinct strategies.

reasons.message: No winning route plays from a board with empty slots. Merely running out on the final winning turn is not a supply decision.
45% of sampled reasonable states are proven dead before final Resolve.
Enemy positions 0, 6 have no spare physical letter supply even under optimistic refill reachability.

warnings.message: 3220 opening spellings and 57774 spellings in the full refill-supply superset have unknown POS; they receive no unsupported grammar category.

6922 opening spellings and 104903 spellings in the full refill-supply superset are unlisted semantically. Neutral gameplay fallback is not proof of unrelated meaning; the superset does not establish future reachability.
3 reasonable states remain unknown; the reported dead-state rate is conditional on assessed states.
The best witnessed solution depth is not a proved minimum.
Search limits were reached; solution counts and opportunity counts are lower bounds.

components.name: solution
components.explanation: A replayed winning witness with room for several turns.

components.name: semanticChoices
components.explanation: Measured semantic counterfactual and exact route replays.

components.name: multipleStrategies
components.explanation: Distinct observed opening/category/special-timing signatures, capped at eight.

components.name: resistedBait
components.explanation: Playable resisted words compete with counters in the opening.

components.name: wardDecisions
components.explanation: Ward changes outcomes or Resolve and has several observed uses.

components.name: strikeDecisions
components.explanation: Strike affects matching hits or outcomes and has several observed uses.

components.name: grammarRelevance
components.explanation: Measured effect of disabling encounter grammar.

components.name: armourRelevance
components.explanation: Armour changes play and has several matching word opportunities.

components.name: refillPlanning
components.explanation: Fraction of observed winning moves using newly refilled physical tiles.

components.name: finiteSupplyChoices
components.explanation: Replayed wins that make further words after refill exhaustion has left empty board slots; final-turn exhaustion alone earns no credit.

components.name: lateSuspense
components.explanation: Assessed sampled final-Resolve positions with at least one direct winning move.

components.name: clutch
components.explanation: Witnessed final-Resolve rescues with annotated fair vocabulary.

components.name: commonVocabulary
components.explanation: Mean familiarity of annotated winning words; unknown coverage is reported separately.

components.name: branching
components.explanation: Several distinct plausible opening words.

components.name: letterRedundancy
components.explanation: Observed alternative matching words for enemy positions.

components.name: tradeoff
components.explanation: Observed sequence tradeoffs, useful bait, or different winning routes.

components.name: prematureHopelessness
components.explanation: Only proven premature dead states incur this penalty; unknowns are separate.

components.name: unknownFairness
components.explanation: Limited fairness evidence incurs a modest uncertainty penalty.

components.name: singlePointDependency
components.explanation: Physical supply has no spare copies even in the optimistic reachable queue.

components.name: obscureWinningWords
components.explanation: Least familiar word in the best fully annotated winning witness; not a global necessity claim.

components.name: semanticIrrelevance
components.explanation: Semantic effects that scarcely affect measured routes are penalized.

components.name: decorativeSpecials
components.explanation: Placed special tiles with negligible measured impact.

components.name: forcedSequence
components.explanation: Only one observed winning strategy; the search may be incomplete.

components.name: trivialWin
components.explanation: A witnessed one-move finish.

components.name: chaoticBranching
components.explanation: Large distinct-word branching makes intended choices less legible.

difficulty.label: HARD
difficulty.evidence: Bounded search: depth is a winning upper bound; route counts are observed lower bounds.
